1.

In terms of the order passed by this Court on 03.01.2024, the prosecutrix and the applicant are present before this Court along with police officials namely Sub Inspector Subba Yadav, Constable Shikha Tripathi and Sub Inspector Umakant Dwivedi.
In terms of the earlier order dated 12.12.2023, the applicant states that he is ready and willing to marry the victim, however the victim has refused to marry the applicant.
In view thereof, their presence is dispensed with.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajesh Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The F.I.R. in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant on the false pretext of marriage and he was helped by his father and brother in enticing away the daughter of the informant.
In the light of the said allegation, the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., wherein she disclosed her age as 17 years and six months.

She also stated that the applicant used to study with her and on the false pretext of marriage, she was taken to Hazipur (Bihar) and thereafter stayed together for a month in a rented accommodation and physical relations were also formed over the said period of time.
Subsequently, the applicant used to beat her and demanded money and subsequently he brought her back on 05.10.2022 and left her at the station and thereafter her parents came and picked her.

In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that on 09.08.2023 after college was over, the applicant along with his father and brother as well as two other relatives including the sister and mother on the false pretext of marriage took her to their home, thereafter, the mother of the applicant administered some medicine and thereafter three persons named in the FIR took her to Bihar and thereafter they kept her in a room and allegation of rape was leveled against all the three persons including the father and the brother of the applicant.
Subsequently on 01.10.2023, she reached Sultanpur, from where her parents took her away.
It was also stated that the applicant was studying with her and were friendly and her mother used to tell her that she would marry her son with the victim.
The medical on record, which was conducted on 07.10.2022 did not reveal any injury on corroboration with the allegations leveled.
As per the High School Certificate, the date of birth of the victim is 13.03.2005, thus on the date of incident, the victim was 17 years and six months of age.
The radiological age as determined is shown as 18 years.
The applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 01.12.2022.
4. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the allegation, the entire case is based upon forming of physical relation on the false pretext of marriage, statement under Section 161 &1 164 Cr.P.C primarily demonstrate that while giving statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the entire family members were implicated including the sister and mother of the applicant.

It is also admitted that the victim had stayed with the applicant for a period of one month at Bihar in a rented accommodation, for which, there is no material as to what steps were taken by the victim for the entire period of one month.

Considering the age of the victim and the law as explained in the case of Deepak Gulati Versus of State of Haryana, AIR 2013 SC 2071 coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 01.12.2022 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Vikash Gupta be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 217 of 2022, under Sections 323, 506, 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Dhanpatganj,
District Sultanpur, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
